LESSON: CONSTRUCTING FRAMED SUSPENDED GARDEN

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: PRODUCTION TECHNIQUES Strand Sub strand Specific learning outcomes Suggested lea
Topic 4.2: Constructing Framed Suspended Garden
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Constructing Framed Suspended Garden, part of PRODUCTION TECHNIQUES Strand Sub strand Specific learning outcomes Suggested lea in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: how to innovate and construct 1. Why do we practise gardening skills? 2.How are framed suspended gardens constructed?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Constructing Framed Suspended Garden together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: The learner develops the skill of connecting with technology as they use digital devices connected to the internet to

search for information, photos, audiovisual clips and illustrations on framed suspended gardens to understand how they are constructed.

42

• Creativity and imagination: The learner develops the skill of decision making as they innovate and construct framed suspended gardens

using locally available materials.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner develops researching skills as they establish a crop on the constructed framed

suspended garden.

Values:
• Unity: As a learner cooperates as they work in groups to construct framed suspended gardens.

• Responsibility: As a learner displays accountability while using workshop tools and equipment to construct the framed suspended

gardens.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Environmental education and climate change: The learner re-use locally available materials to construct framed suspended gardens.

• Safety and Security: The learners observe safety for self and others as they use workshop tools and equipment to construct framed

suspended gardens.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner relate value addition concept to commodity marketing learnt in Pre-technical Studies.
